Consider the system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}\,\,3x-3y=1 \\ -x+2y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the unknown $y$ can be written as $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|}$, where ${D}_{y}=$
feedback.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}\,\,3x-3y=1 \\ -x+2y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}3 & \,\,1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$
